bound_statement.input: two finite line families L,M in F^3 with |L|<=|M| and |L|=O(p^2) in characteristic p
bound_statement.degeneracy: no quadric contains simultaneously s lines of L and t lines of M
bound_statement.surface_choice: interpolate a degree D=O(|L|^(1/2)) surface containing every line in L
bound_statement.degree_condition: the imported c0 cutoff guarantees component degrees below characteristic in the positive-characteristic branch

absorption_ledger.off_surface_M_lines: each M-line not contained in the interpolating surface contributes at most D points by Bezout
absorption_ledger.plane_quadric_components: charged by the stated s,t quadric degeneracy ledger
absorption_ledger.singly_ruled_components: ordinary contained lines meet O(d_i) peers; exceptional directrix lines are O(1) and already charged
absorption_ledger.non_ruled_components: Cayley-Salmon now gives Flec(F_i) nonzero; Bezout yields O(d_i^3) internal line-intersection scale
absorption_ledger.component_degree_sum: sum d_i<=D and the closed component ledger absorbs O(sum d_i^3) into the same target scale under the previous certificate's accounting
absorption_ledger.result: all contributions match the bipartite Guth-Katz/Kollar target bound

remaining_atoms.why_remaining: the now-closed line-intersection theorem must be reinserted into de Zeeuw's point-plane incidence reduction
